cards.title: 2.1 Cash (bookkeeping semester)
body: Cash is the asset thieves and errors love. Control: separate duties, receipts banked intact, payments by cheque where possible, surprise counts.
**Petty cash** — small notes and coins for tiny purchases (taxi, stamps). Imprest system: start with a fixed float; at top-up, replenish exactly what was spent.

Exam-style F — petty cash
cards.problem: Imprest = 400 Nfa. Vouchers: taxi 40, pens 25, tea 15. Journalise the replenishment.

steps.text: Cash left in tin should be 320.
Replenish 80 Nfa from the bank / cashier.
Dr Transport 40; Dr Stationery 25; Dr Refreshments 15; Cr Cash/Bank 80.
Do *not* debit Petty cash again unless you are changing the float size.

cards.answer: Do *not* debit Petty cash again unless you are changing the float size.

cards.title: Cash – Meaning and its Importance
body: Bank statement vs cash book: ticks for matching items; then outstanding cheques, unrecorded deposits, bank charges, direct deposits. The adjusted cash-book balance should equal the adjusted bank statement.

cards.title: 2.1.1 Control of Cash
body: The major step in achieving internal control over cash transactions and cash balances include separating the function of handling cash from the maintenance of accounting records.
Cash transactions can be broadly divided into cash receipts and cash disbursements.
The term ‘cash receipts’ refers to cash coming into the business from cash sales, collection of receivables, bank loans, sale of assets, and from other sources.
The term cash disbursement refers to cash payments made by the business for cash purchases, payment of accounts payable, payment of expenses, payment of bank loans, etc.

cards.title: 2.1.2 Petty Cash Fund
body: A petty cash fund is a small cash fund kept in the office for the purposes of making miscellaneous payments.

The operation of a petty cash fund, often called an imprest system (the term “imprest” means an advance of money for a designated purpose), involves three steps: (a) establishing the fund, (b) making payments from the fund, and (c) replenishing the fund.
The fund custodian cashes the cheque and places the proceeds in a locked petty cash box or drawer.
When the custodian of the fund cashes the cheque, the Cash account of business is decreased and the Petty Cash account, another asset account, is increased.

cards.title: 2.1.3 Opening a Chequing Account
body: The person or business in whose name cash is deposited is called a depositor.
A bank account from which payments can be ordered by a depositor is called a Chequing account.
A business paper used to make payments from a Chequing account is known as a Cheque.
As a depositor, the is businessperson able to authorize the bank to pay money to the person or firm whose name appears on the cheque.

cards.title: 2.1.4 Bank Statements
body: A list of paid cheques in numerical order by cheque sequence number along with the date of payment and amount.
Other debits and credits made during the month.
All checks that have been received for payment and paid by the bank are sent back to the business along with the bank statement.
Service charges are often identified on the bank statement by a code symbol such as SC.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following items is strictly excluded from being classified as 'Cash' on a company's balance sheet?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Define what constitutes cash**
In accounting, cash includes physical currency, coins, and any negotiable instrument that a bank will accept for immediate deposit and credit. This includes money orders, travelers' cheques, and bank drafts.

**Step 2: Evaluate the exception**
A postdated cheque is a cheque dated in the future. Because banks will not accept it for immediate deposit and credit until that future date arrives, it is not readily convertible to cash and is classified as a receivable instead.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, **Postdated cheques** are excluded from Cash.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: In cash operations, the rule that the employee who physical handles cash must never have access to the cash accounting records is an application of:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall internal control principles**
Internal control includes several principles: segregation of duties, establishment of responsibility, physical controls, and independent verification.

**Step 2: Match the rule to the principle**
Separating the physical custody of an asset (cashier handling cash) from its recording (accountant maintaining records) is the classic definition of **Segregation of Duties**.

**Step 3: Final Result**
This represents **Segregation of duties**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is a petty cash fund?

options.A: Cash kept in the office for making small payments
options.B: Cash kept in the bank for making small payments
options.C: Cash kept in the office for payroll (salary) payment
options.D: Cash collected from customers and kept in the cash register
options.E: Cash from which payment by check is made

cards.why: Petty cash is a small amount of **physical cash kept on hand** at the business location to pay for minor expenses (postage, office snacks, taxis) where writing a check is impractical.

cards.title: 2.2 Payroll
body: Gross pay → minus deductions (tax, pension, other) → net pay. Employer may also owe extra payroll taxes / contributions. Journal: debit wage expense (gross), credit liabilities for each deduction and credit cash/bank for the net.

cards.problem: Gross monthly pay 6,000 Nfa. Income tax 600, pension 300 (employee). Employer pension 300 extra. Record the salary journal and the employer contribution.

Employer extra: Dr Pension expense 300; Cr Pension payable 300.
When paid to the tax/pension office, debit the payable accounts and credit cash.

cards.answer: When paid to the tax/pension office, debit the payable accounts and credit cash.

cards.title: 2.2.1 Introduction
body: One expense that most businesses incur is payroll expense.
A list of employees showing the salaries or wages due to them for a certain work period such as a week or a month is called a payroll.

cards.title: 2.2.2 Payroll Accounting System
body: Accounting for the cost of labour begins with the establishment of a payroll system.
When an employee is initially hired, his /her personal record is established. i.e. the employee’s address, birth date, work experience, education, etc. are all recorded.
In large companies, the personnel file is maintained by the personnel department.
Employers pay employees daily, weekly, biweekly, or monthly.

cards.title: 2.2.3 Payment of payroll liabilities
body: Recording the total expense and the total liabilities in the general journal.
The next part of the process involves the payment of the employees.
The cheque method is simpler and safer for the business.
The cheques are then sent to the financial manager’s (treasurer’s) office for signature.

cards.title: 2.2.4 Control over payroll system
body: The individual paychecks prepared by the payroll division are signed by the financial manager (treasurer), then reviewed and co-signed by another executive.
The internal auditor must be constantly on guard against both errors and fraud.
The separation of duties is the key in controlling payroll system.
The people in the personnel department should not be allowed to prepare payrolls or write checks.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: When replenishing a petty cash fund, if the sum of cash remaining in the box plus the total vouchers is less than the established fund size, the shortage is debited to:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Understand petty cash discrepancies**
When actual cash plus vouchers in a petty cash box is less than the established fund size, a shortage exists.

**Step 2: Identify the accounting entry**
This shortage is debited to the **Cash Over or Short** account, which acts as a miscellaneous operating expense.

**Step 3: Final Result**
The shortage is debited to the **Cash Over or Short account**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following reconciling items in a bank reconciliation statement does NOT require an adjusting journal entry on the company's books?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Determine which side of the reconciliation requires entries**
In a bank reconciliation, only the reconciling items on the *book* side (depositor's ledger side) require adjusting journal entries. Bank-side adjustments clear naturally over time.

**Step 2: Evaluate the options**
- Service charges, NSF cheques, and notes collected are unknown to the book until the statement arrives, thus requiring book-side adjustments and journal entries.
- Outstanding cheques are already recorded by the company but not yet by the bank; they adjust the *bank* side and do not require adjusting entries.

**Step 3: Final Result**
**Outstanding cheques** do not require adjusting entries.

cards.q: A reconciling item that requires a journal entry on the books of the company is:
cards.why: Only items that affect the **Book balance** (the company's records) require journal entries. These include **NSF checks, bank service charges, interest earned, and notes collected by the bank**.

cards.title: 2.3 Plant assets and depreciation
body: Plant / fixed assets: land, buildings, machines, vehicles — used for more than one year, not bought to resell. Land is usually *not* depreciated.
Straight-line (the exam favourite):
Annual dep. = (Cost − Residual value) / Useful life in years

cards.title: Only the 40,000 that will be used up is depreciated.
Exam-style H — straight line
cards.problem: Machine cost 50,000 Nfa, residual 10,000 Nfa, life 4 years. Find annual depreciation, book value after 2 years, and the year-end journal.

steps.text: Depreciable amount = 50,000 − 10,000 = 40,000.
After 2 years accumulated dep. = 20,000.
Journal each year: Dr Depreciation expense 10,000; Cr Accumulated depreciation 10,000.
On the statement: Machine 50,000 less Accum. dep. 20,000 = 30,000 net.
Never credit the asset account itself under this method.

cards.answer: Never credit the asset account itself under this method.

cards.title: 2.3.1 Introduction
body: An operating cycle is the length of time between (1) purchase of services or merchandise (products) from suppliers to carry out a business’s activities, and (2) the sale of services or merchandise (products) to customers.
If an item is held for resale to customers, it should be classified as an inventory (current asset) – not plant assets – no matter how durable it is.

For example, a computer that is held for sale by an electronic equipment retailer would be considered inventory, whereas the same computer would be considered a non-current asset for a printing company that buys it for use in operations.
Intangible assets are long term assets which are used in the operation of the business that do not have physical substance and in most cases have to do with legal rights and advantages held.

cards.title: 2.3.2 Accountable events in the lives of plant assets
body: For all categories of plant assets, there are three basic accountable events: (A) acquisition, (B) allocation of the acquisition cost to expense over the asset’s useful life (depreciation), and (C) sale or disposal.
The cost principle requires that companies record plant assets at cost (historical cost).
Cost consists of all expenditures reasonable and necessary for getting the asset to the desired location and ready for its intended use.
For example, the cost of installing and testing a machine is a legitimate cost of the machine.

cards.title: 2.3.3 Controlling plant assets
body: Good internal control requires that each plant asset be separately identified usually with a unique identification number that is either engraved on the asset or attached with a permanent sticker or tag.
Periodically, an inventory of plant assets should be taken to verify the existence, location, condition, and continued use of each asset.
For good internal control, the custodians of the assets must not have access to the records.

In keeping these records, companies usually divide their plant assets into functional groups and provide each group with a separate asset account and accumulated depreciation account in the General Ledger.

cards.title: 2.3.4 Statement presentation of a plant asset and its depreciation
body: Plant assets are shown in the balance sheet at their book values (or carrying values).
Accumulated depreciation is a contra-asset account, representing that portion of the asset’s cost that has already been allocated to expenses.
The depreciation methods in use should be disclosed in the notes to the financial statements as per the full disclosure principle.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: A customer's cheque that is deposited but returned by the bank because the customer's bank account balance is insufficient is recorded by the depositor as:

options.C: Debit Bank Service Charges, Credit Cash

cards.why:
**Step 1: Identify the impact of an NSF cheque**
When a customer's deposited check bounces (NSF), the bank deducts the money from the company's account. This reverses the previous receipt.

**Step 2: Formulate the journal entry**
The company must reduce its cash balance (Credit Cash) and re-establish the customer's debt (Debit Accounts Receivable).

**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct entry is **Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Cash**.

cards.title: Step-by-step
cards.problem: A customer's cheque that is deposited but returned by the bank because the customer's bank account balance is insufficient is recorded by the depositor as:

steps.text: **Step 1: Identify the impact of an NSF cheque**
When a customer's deposited check bounces (NSF), the bank deducts the money from the company's account. This reverses the previous receipt.
**Step 2: Formulate the journal entry**
The company must reduce its cash balance (Credit Cash) and re-establish the customer's debt (Debit Accounts Receivable).
**Step 3: Final Result**
The correct entry is **Debit Accounts Receivable, Credit Cash**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Under the Eritrean Labor Proclamation currently in effect (Proclamation 118/2001), overtime hours worked during weekly rest days are paid at:
cards.why:
**Step 1: Review Eritrean labor laws on overtime**
Proclamation 118/2001 (Article 48) establishes progressive rates for overtime hours based on when they are worked.

**Step 2: Match the rate to weekly rest days**
- 1.25x is for daytime overtime.
- 1.5x is for nighttime overtime.
- 2.0x is for weekly rest days (weekends).
- 2.5x is for public holidays.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Weekly rest day overtime is paid at **2.0 times the base hourly rate**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: According to the Eritrean labor proclamation currently in effect, the over time rate for overtime hours worked during weekly rest days is
cards.why:
Under Eritrean Labor Law, different overtime rates apply depending on when the work is done:
- Night work (10 PM - 6 AM): 1.5 times the hourly rate.
- Weekly rest day: **2.0 (Double)** the hourly rate.
- Public holidays: 2.5 times the hourly rate.

tips.text: Cash is the most liquid asset of all the assets of a business. As a result, it offers the greatest temptation for theft.
Therefore, business managers have the responsibility to ensure that there is proper accounting for cash receipts and disbursements so as to prevent loss of cash from fraud or theft.
In this sub-unit, we have discussed crucial tools that businesses can use to protect and account for cash.

We have discussed that good internal control over cash requires that all receipts be deposited in the bank as soon as they are collected and making all payments by cheque; except for smaller cash payments which are usually made from a petty cash fund.
This sub-unit has shown that the use of the banking systems gives the advantage of dual recording for a business’s cash transactions.
One record is kept by the business as part of its accounting system. Another is kept by the bank which should be the exact mirror record of the business’s cash transactions.

Finally, we have illustrated that the bank reconciliation helps to disclose internal control failures, such as unauthorized cash disbursements or failures to deposit cash receipts, as well as errors in either the bank or the depositor’s accounting records.
For many business organizations payroll represents a large share of total costs.
The internal control of businesses and the government require detailed payroll records for employees.
First, employees are sensitive about their pay and therefore, error free payroll preparation becomes important to maintain their satisfaction.

why: Answer B: 9,000

questions.q: One of the following is **not** true concerning the Eritrean payroll system?

options.A: The amount recorded as salary and wages expense is the sum of the gross pay amounts for all employees.
options.B: The contractual amount which an employee earns during a pay period is referred to as gross earnings.
options.C: The rate of the pension fund of the State of Eritrea is 5% of basic salary.
options.D: The journal entry for the net amount paid to employees involves a credit to salaries and wages payable.
options.E: Salaried employees earn a fixed amount each pay period.

why: Option D is incorrect because the final payment entry involves a **debit** to Salaries and Wages Payable (to close the liability) and a **credit to Cash** (money leaving the business). Crediting the liability would imply the debt is increasing.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: The petty cash fund had an initial imprest balance of $$ $300 $$. The cash left in box equals $$ $60 $$ and petty cash receipts totaling $$ $250 $$ for office supplies. The entry to replenish the fund would contain a

options.A: credit to Cash Over or Short for $$ $10 $$.
options.C: debit to Cash short & over for $$ $10 $$.

why:
**Step 1: Calculate cash needed.** 
Fund Size ($$ 300 $$) - Cash Left ($$ 60 $$) = $$ $240 $$ needed from main bank.
**Step 2: Compare with receipts.** 
Total Receipts = $$ $250 $$. 
**Step 3: Analyze.** 
The accountant has $$ $250 $$ in expense receipts but only needs $$ $240 $$ to bring the box back to $$ $300 $$. This means there is $$ $10 $$ **more cash** than there should be (Overage).
**Step 4: Journal Entry.** 
Dr. Expenses ($$ 250 $$); Cr. Cash ($$ 240 $$); **Cr. Cash Over or Short ($$ 10 $$)**.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: When recording payroll,

options.A: payroll deductions are recorded as salaries and wages expense.
options.B: gross earnings are recorded as salaries and wages payable.
options.C: payroll deductions are recorded in the appropriate liability accounts.
options.D: net pay is recorded as salaries and wages expense.

why:
**Payroll Journal Entry Logic:**
1. **Debit:** Salaries and Wages Expense (for the **Gross Amount**).
2. **Credit:** Various **Liability Accounts** (for the deductions like Income Tax Payable, Pension Payable).
3. **Credit:** Salaries and Wages Payable or Cash (for the **Net Amount**).
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Petty cash account is credited when

options.A: the petty cash fund is established.
options.B: the petty cash size is increasing.
options.C: the petty cash size is decreasing.
options.E: cash is paid from the petty cash fund.

why: Under the imprest system, the Petty Cash **asset account** is only touched (debited or credited) when the fund is first established, or when its permanent size is changed. If the company decides to **decrease the size** of the fund, the account is **credited**.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which of the following items constitutes a good cash control device?
why: All listed items are essential for internal control of cash. **Petty cash control** manages small payments; **Bank reconciliation** ensures bank and book balances match; and **Separation of duties** prevents fraud by ensuring no single person controls all parts of a transaction.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: The deductions from an employee gross pay are recorded by the business as:
why: Amounts withheld from an employee's pay (like taxes or pension) are **liabilities** for the business because the company owes that money to the government or other agencies until they are paid.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Cash shortages are **not** discovered because there are no daily cash counts by supervisors. This is an example of the internal control principle called:
why: Independent internal verification involves the review, comparison, and reconciliation of data prepared by employees. A supervisor counting cash to verify the cashier's work is 'independent internal verification'.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Which of the following items appears on the bank side of bank reconciliation?
why: In a bank reconciliation, **Deposits in Transit** and **Outstanding Checks** are adjustments made to the **Bank Statement balance** because the bank is not yet aware of these transactions recorded by the company.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: A company writes a check to replenish a $$ $200 $$ petty cash fund when the fund contains receipts of $$ $194 $$ and $$ $8 $$ in cash. In recording the check, the company should

options.A: Debit Cash Over and Short for $2.

why:
**Step 1: Calculate amount needed to replenish.**
Initial fund = $$ 200 $$. Cash remaining = $$ 8 $$. 
Amount needed = $$ 200 - 8 = 192 $$.
**Step 2: Check for discrepancies.**
Receipts ($$ 194 $$) + Cash ($$ 8 $$) = $$ 202 $$. 
Since we have $$ 202 $$ but should have only $$ 200 $$, we have a $$ $2 $$ **overage**.
**Step 3: Journal Entry.**
Debit Expenses 194; Credit Cash Over and Short 2; **Credit Cash 192**.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: Semhar Metal Work writes a check to replenish a petty cash fund of 500 Nakfa when the fund contains receipts of Nakfa 494 and Nakfa 4 in cash. In recording the check, the company should:

options.B: debit cash short and over for Nakfa 2
options.D: debit cash short and over for Nakfa 6

why:
**Step 1:** Total accounted for = Receipts (494) + Cash on hand (4) = 498 Nakfa.
**Step 2:** The fund should be 500 Nakfa. 
**Step 3:** Difference = 500 - 498 = 2 Nakfa (Shortage).
**Step 4:** To replenish, the company debits expenses for 494 and debits **Cash Short and Over** for 2 to balance the entry against the check amount.
questions.tip: Read every option before choosing; rule out the ones that contradict the notes.

questions.q: According to Labor Proclamation of Eritrea, an employee who works overtime between 10:00 pm and 6:00 am in the morning is entitled to a rate of:
why: Under the Eritrean Labor Proclamation, overtime worked during the night (usually defined between 10:00 pm and 6:00 am) is compensated at **1.5 times** (one and a half) the regular hourly rate.
